identity.name: Web-Based Indirect Prompt Injection Against a Browsing AI Agent — DOM-Hidden Payload Drives Autonomous Action (SIM-BROWSER-006)
identity.summary: A browsing AI agent visits an attacker page whose instructions are hidden in the DOM (zero-sized, off-screen, opacity 0, white-on-white, obfuscated). It ingests them and, with no human gesture, performs a cross-origin payment/OAuth action or a data leak. The catch is the page-load -> hidden-ingest -> unattended-action causality chain plus egress to the published IDPI domains.
identity.description: Unit 42 documented in-the-wild web-based indirect prompt injection (IDPI) against autonomous browsing agents: benign-looking pages carry instructions the human never sees but the agent's DOM/innerText scan ingests. The payload is concealed with CSS (font-size:0/line-height:0, position:absolute;left:-9999px, display:none, visibility:hidden, opacity:0, color:#ffffff on #ffffff), hidden <textarea> and data-* attribute cloaking, SVG/XML CDATA, canvas-rendered (OCR-only) text, and runtime base64 decode with timed delays; the instruction text itself is obfuscated with zero-width Unicode, Cyrillic/Greek homoglyphs, U+202E bidi override, HTML-entity (I) and URL (%49) encoding, nested encoding chains, and payload-splitting across elements. Observed hijacked actions: approval override on an ad-review agent (reviewerpress[.]com), 'delete your database' (splintered[.]co[.]uk), contact-list theft (dylansparks[.]com), forced donation/payment to buy.stripe[.]com and paypal[.]me/shiftypumpkin, an unattended Google OAuth consent + Pro-plan subscription (llm7-landing.pages[.]dev -> token.llm7[.]io), system-prompt exfiltration, and destructive backend command attempts (fork bomb / recursive-delete strings present as page text on cblanke2.pages[.]dev). This card models that on the BROWSER plane and validates the Cortex catch. Because every tool the agent uses is legitimate (its own navigator, its own network stack), a hand-authored signature misses it — so the emphasis is behavioral: two auto-tuned ABIOCs anchor on the causality chain rather than a bad string. ABIOC A fires when, within one agent session, an untrusted page load is followed by a hidden-DOM ingest and then a cross-origin navigation to a sensitive-origin class (payment/OAuth/LLM-billing) that is absent from the agent's task manifest — the learned baseline is that the agent only reaches sensitive origins it was tasked with, so an off-manifest sensitive navigation right after ingesting concealed page content is the anomaly (not the mere absence of a human gesture, which an unattended agent never produces). ABIOC B fires when a browser-engine process (chrome/chromium/chromium-browser/headless_shell — generic node workers excluded) parents an OS shell after a page load — a lineage a browser engine's learned profile never exhibits, which is exactly what the injected backend-command attempts produce. A validation XQL surfaces the gesture-less navigation; a hunting XQL keys Advanced DNS Security on resolutions to the published IDPI and payment domains; a correlation rule stitches the browser deviation and the egress on one agent_hostname + browser_session_id into a single IDPI incident the DC presents as proof Cortex caught an unattended agent hijack no static rule was written for.

campaigns: In-the-wild web-based indirect prompt injection (IDPI) against autonomous browsing agents — 22 distinct payload-engineering techniques; 75.8% single-injection pages, 85.2% social-engineering jailbreaks, 73.2% on .com (Unit 42, 2025-2026)

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM Linux agent (and Prisma Browser telemetry where available) installed so browsing-agent process lineage and navigation/network telemetry reach xdr_data / prisma_browser_events.

A browsing-agent identity (e.g. a Node/Playwright headless agent running as 'node') exists whose learned Cortex profile is unattended automation with no interactive shell and no gesture-less sensitive-origin navigation.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE. Models the IDPI causality chain: browsing agent loads an
# attacker page carrying a DOM-hidden instruction, then performs an autonomous
# (no-human-gesture) cross-origin action and a browser->shell lineage. Nothing
# destructive is executed; the injected backend command is left as an inert
# SAFE-MODE marker (never run).
set -euo pipefail
MARK="${MARKER_DIR:-/tmp}/cortexsim-browser-006"
# (1) Agent fetches the attacker IDPI page (page-load + egress signal).
curl -s --max-time 5 "http://${STAGE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/idpi/advertorial" -o "${MARK}.page" 2>/dev/null || true
# (2) Autonomous cross-origin action with no human gesture: instead of a real
#     payment/OAuth, drop a marker recording the redirect the injection forces.
curl -s --max-time 5 "http://${STAGE_HOST:-127.0.0.1}/pay/checkout" -o "${MARK}.autonomous-action" 2>/dev/null || true
# (3) Browser->shell lineage: the injected backend-command attempt. Recorded as
#     an inert SAFE-MODE marker string; the destructive payload is NOT executed.
printf 'SAFE-MODE: injected backend-command attempt (recursive-delete / fork-bomb class) neutralized — not executed\n' > "${MARK}.injected-command.SAFE-MODE"
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-BROWSER-006 IDPI causality chain emitted (non-destructive).'

abiocs.name: Browsing Agent Sensitive-Origin Action After Hidden-DOM Ingest Outside Task Manifest
abiocs.description: Within one browsing-agent session, an untrusted page load is followed by ingestion of non-rendered DOM content (hidden / off-screen / zero-size / transparent) and then a cross-origin navigation to a sensitive-origin class (payment / OAuth-consent / LLM-billing) that was NOT present in the agent's task/instruction manifest. The ABIOC anchors on the page-load -> hidden-DOM-ingest -> off-manifest sensitive-navigation causality chain correlated by browser_session_id, not on any bad URL string and not on the mere absence of a human gesture (an unattended agent never produces gestures, so gesture-less navigation is its baseline, not the anomaly). The learned baseline is that the agent only reaches sensitive origins that appear in its task manifest; the injection adds an off-manifest sensitive navigation immediately after it ingests concealed page content. It generalizes to any sensitive origin the agent reaches off-manifest after a hidden-DOM ingest, catching the IDPI hijack even though every binary the agent uses is legitimate.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = prisma_browser_events
| filter actor_effective_username in ("node", "www-data", "nobody")
| filter event_type in ("page_load", "dom_content_ingest", "navigation")
| alter untrusted_page_load = if(event_type = "page_load" and page_origin_trust = "untrusted", 1, 0)
| alter hidden_dom_ingest = if(event_type = "dom_content_ingest" and dom_visibility in ("hidden", "offscreen", "zero_size", "transparent"), 1, 0)
| alter offmanifest_sensitive_nav = if(event_type = "navigation" and cross_origin = true and dest_origin_class = "sensitive" and in_task_manifest = false, 1, 0)
| comp sum(untrusted_page_load) as untrusted_loads, sum(hidden_dom_ingest) as hidden_ingests, sum(offmanifest_sensitive_nav) as offmanifest_navs, min(_time) as chain_start, max(_time) as chain_end by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, browser_session_id
| filter untrusted_loads >= 1 and hidden_ingests >= 1 and offmanifest_navs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, browser_session_id, untrusted_loads, hidden_ingests, offmanifest_navs
abiocs.causality_anchor: Untrusted page load in the agent session -> ingestion of non-rendered/hidden DOM content -> cross-origin navigation to a sensitive-origin class that is absent from the agent's task manifest, all correlated on browser_session_id. The injected instruction that drives an off-manifest sensitive navigation right after a hidden-DOM ingest — not a human gesture and not a known-bad domain list — is what the chain isolates.

abiocs.name: Browsing Agent Process Spawns Shell After DOM-Hidden Ingest
abiocs.description: A browser-engine process (chrome/chromium/chromium-browser/headless_shell) parents an OS shell shortly after loading a page — the lineage the injected backend-command attempts (recursive-delete / fork-bomb class) produce. The parent set is scoped to actual browser-engine images only; generic 'node' workers are deliberately excluded because Node.js shelling out to /bin/sh (child_process.exec, npm/yarn scripts) is ubiquitous and benign, so a node->sh match cannot carry this detection. A browser engine's learned per-process profile never spawns an interpreter, so the ABIOC fires on the browser-engine->shell lineage deviation anchored to the page load, not on any command string.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("chrome", "chromium", "chromium-browser", "headless_shell")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("chrome", "chromium", "chromium-browser", "headless_shell")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "python3")
| filter actor_effective_username in ("node", "www-data", "nobody")
| comp count() as agent_spawned_shells by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter agent_spawned_shells >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_instance_id, agent_spawned_shells
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned browsing-agent baseline (never parents an OS interpreter) -> IDPI page load and DOM-hidden ingest -> browsing-agent process spawns sh/bash for the injected backend-command attempt, anchored to the agent process lineage.

xql_queries.name: SIM-BROWSER-006 Autonomous Cross-Origin Navigation Surfaced
xql_queries.query:
dataset = prisma_browser_events
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter actor_effective_username in ("node", "www-data", "nobody")
| filter event_type = "navigation" and cross_origin = true and dest_origin_class = "sensitive"
| filter in_task_manifest = false and preceded_by_hidden_dom_ingest = true
| comp count() as offmanifest_sensitive_navs by agent_hostname, browser_session_id
| filter offmanifest_sensitive_navs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, browser_session_id, offmanifest_sensitive_navs

xql_queries.name: SIM-BROWSER-006 IDPI Domain and Payment Egress Hunt
xql_queries.query:
dataset = pan_dns
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter dns_query_name in ("reviewerpress.com", "splintered.co.uk", "dylansparks.com", "llm7-landing.pages.dev", "cblanke2.pages.dev", "storage3d.com", "buy.stripe.com", "token.llm7.io", "1winofficialsite.in", "perceptivepumpkin.com", "shiftypumpkin.com")
| comp count() as idpi_lookups by agent_hostname, dns_query_name
| filter idpi_lookups >= 1
| sort desc idpi_lookups
| fields agent_hostname, dns_query_name, idpi_lookups

correlation_rules.name: Web-Based Indirect Prompt Injection Incident — Browsing-Agent Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Browsing Agent Sensitive-Origin Action After Hidden-DOM Ingest Outside Task Manifest) AND (ABIOC(Browsing Agent Process Spawns Shell After DOM-Hidden Ingest) OR XQL(SIM-BROWSER-006 IDPI Domain and Payment Egress Hunt)) — fuses the off-manifest sensitive-origin action that follows a hidden-DOM ingest, the browser-engine-parents-shell lineage, and the IDPI/payment egress on the same agent_hostname and browser_session_id within a 5-minute window into a single web-based indirect-prompt-injection incident anchored to the page-load -> hidden-ingest -> off-manifest-navigation causality chain.

use_cases.name: Web-Based Indirect Prompt Injection Against a Browsing AI Agent
use_cases.description: Cortex behavioral analytics and Advanced DNS Security catch a browsing AI agent hijacked by DOM-hidden instructions on an attacker page: the agent performs an unattended cross-origin payment/OAuth action and a browser-parented shell attempt, anchored to the page-load-to-hidden-ingest-to-no-gesture causality chain, where no static rule was written for the legitimate agent binaries involved.

test_cases.objective: The browsing agent's off-manifest cross-origin action to a sensitive (payment/OAuth) origin — reached right after it ingests hidden DOM content — fires ABIOC A and is surfaced by the validation XQL.
preconditions: Browser/EDR target with the Cortex agent (and Prisma Browser telemetry where available).
Baseline window elapsed with the browsing agent reaching only task-manifest sensitive origins.
steps: Drive the browsing agent onto the IDPI page so it ingests the DOM-hidden instruction.
Observe the agent perform a cross-origin navigation to a sensitive origin absent from its task manifest immediately after the hidden-DOM ingest.
Confirm ABIOC A fires and the validation XQL returns the off-manifest sensitive navigation.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Browsing Agent Sensitive-Origin Action After Hidden-DOM Ingest Outside Task Manifest` fires.
XQL `SIM-BROWSER-006 Autonomous Cross-Origin Navigation Surfaced` returns >= 1 row for the agent session.

test_cases.objective: The browsing-agent process parenting an OS shell (the injected backend-command lineage) fires ABIOC B.
preconditions: EDR target with the Cortex Linux agent installed.
Browsing-agent identity whose learned profile never parents an interpreter.
steps: Let the IDPI page inject a backend-command instruction (SAFE-MODE; not executed).
Observe the browsing-agent process attempt to spawn sh/bash.
Confirm ABIOC B fires on the browser->shell lineage deviation.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Browsing Agent Process Spawns Shell After DOM-Hidden Ingest` fires.
The alert is anchored to the browsing-agent process lineage, not a command-string signature.

test_cases.objective: Correlation stitches the browser deviations and the IDPI/payment egress into one incident; Advanced DNS Security flags the domain resolutions.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs available and DNS telemetry (pan_dns) reaching the tenant.
Egress to the emulated IDPI/payment staging host authorised.
steps: Run the full IDPI causality chain (page load -> autonomous action -> browser->shell).
Observe CR-BROWSER-0006 raise one incident on the agent session.
Confirm the DNS hunt / Advanced DNS Security surfaces resolutions to the IDPI/payment domains.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-BROWSER-0006` raises one stitched web-based indirect-prompt-injection incident.
XQL `SIM-BROWSER-006 IDPI Domain and Payment Egress Hunt` (or Advanced DNS Security) surfaces the IDPI/payment domain resolutions.

preventive_controls: Require a human-in-the-loop confirmation gesture before a browsing agent performs any payment, OAuth consent, or cross-origin credentialed action; deny unattended sensitive-origin navigation.

Run browsing agents inside Prisma Browser / remote browser isolation so untrusted web content is separated from the agent's trusted instruction channel (spotlighting), and strip non-rendered DOM (zero-sized, off-screen, opacity-0, hidden <textarea>, data-* payloads) before the agent's context ingest.
Block/sinkhole resolution of known IDPI and abused-payment domains with Advanced DNS Security and Advanced URL Filtering; scope agent egress to an allowlist.
Constrain the browsing-agent service identity so it cannot spawn an OS shell or reach payment/OAuth origins outside an explicit allowlist.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs on the browsing-agent's learned navigation-gesture and per-process baseline rather than hand-authoring signatures for the legitimate agent binaries.

Alert on any cross-origin sensitive-origin (payment / OAuth / LLM-billing) navigation that is absent from the agent's task manifest and follows a hidden/non-rendered DOM ingest in the same agent session — not on the absence of a human gesture, which an unattended agent never produces.
Alert on a browser-engine process (chrome/chromium/chromium-browser/headless_shell) parenting an OS interpreter; do not key on generic node->shell, which is ubiquitous and benign.
Hunt DNS/egress for resolutions to the published IDPI and abused-payment domains and stitch them to the agent session via correlation.
